title: How is a correction of an issued Bills of Lading and Transport Documents document charged?
content:
## Scope

This Bills of Lading and Transport Documents clause set decides which fee, if any, a correction of an issued transport document carries. It applies to each executed correction request after issuance; corrections before issuance are free under the draft approval rules and are not charged here.

## Formal clauses

1. A change of the named consignee after issuance is charged the tier's consignee change fee.
2. Any other correction after issuance is free while the number of corrections after issuance already on the document is below the tier's free correction allowance. Otherwise it costs the tier's correction fee after issuance when the vessel has not departed, or the tier's correction fee after departure when the vessel has departed. The corrections after issuance are counted as the completed correction requests on the document created on or after its date of issue, not counting the request being handled.
3. A correction caused by the line's own keying error against the shipping instructions is never charged.
4. A correction fee is booked only on a document whose status is issued.
5. Each correction request is charged at most once.

## Decision table

| Kind of correction after issuance | Keying error by the line? | Earlier post-issuance corrections versus free allowance | Vessel departed? | Fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Any | Yes | any | any | None |
| Consignee change | No | not relevant | any | The tier's consignee change fee |
| Other particular | No | below the allowance | any | None |
| Other particular | No | at or above the allowance | No | The tier's correction fee after issuance |
| Other particular | No | at or above the allowance | Yes | The tier's correction fee after departure |

## Worked cases (hypothetical tier with a free allowance of two and fees labelled A before departure and D after departure)

- The first post-issuance correction, of the notify party, before departure: no earlier corrections, which is below the allowance of two, so it is free.
- A second correction, of the cargo description, after departure: one earlier correction, still below the allowance, so it is free.
- A third correction, of the package count, before departure: two earlier corrections, which is not below the allowance, so fee A applies; had the vessel departed, fee D would apply.
- The same third correction caused by the line's own keying error against the shipping instructions: no fee.

## Points of judgement

- A consignee change is charged its own fee in place of the correction fee; the free allowance is written for "any other correction" and does not make a consignee change free.
- A fee row is never booked twice for the same correction request, and never on a document that is not issued.
